stories.headline: Musk Unveils $20-25B TERAFAB Chip Factory as Tesla, SpaceX, xAI Joint Venture

key_facts.fact: Elon Musk announced TERAFAB on March 21 at Austin's Seaholm Power Plant — a $20-25 billion joint venture between Tesla, SpaceX, and xAI to build the largest chip manufacturing facility ever, targeting one terawatt of computing power annually.
key_facts.excerpt: Tesla and SpaceX have unveiled 'Terafab,' a joint $25 billion chip fabrication facility in Austin, Texas, that Elon Musk claims will produce 1 terawatt of computing power annually. It would be the largest semiconductor fab ever built — by an absurd margin.

key_facts.fact: TERAFAB is targeting 2-nanometer process technology with initial output of 100,000 wafer starts per month, scaling to 1 million — roughly 70% of TSMC's entire current global output — and producing 100 to 200 billion custom AI chips per year.
key_facts.excerpt: Tesla is targeting 2-nanometer process technology... The production targets are staggering. Terafab is designed for an initial output of 100,000 wafer starts per month, with ambitions to scale to 1 million wafer starts per month at full capacity. For context, that full-scale target would represent roughly 70% of TSMC's entire current global output.

key_facts.fact: Two chip types will be produced: the Tesla AI5 for vehicles and Optimus robots, and the D3 chip for space-based AI data centers. SpaceX filed an FCC application for up to one million AI data center satellites, each providing approximately 100 megawatts of computing capacity.
key_facts.excerpt: SpaceX filed an FCC application in late January seeking approval for up to one million satellites dedicated to AI orbital data center applications.

key_facts.fact: Musk called it 'the most epic chip building exercise in history by far' and said 'We either build the Terafab or we don't have the chips, and we need the chips, so we're going to build the Terafab.' Production is expected to begin in 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: 'We either build the Terafab or we don't have the chips,' Musk said during the event. 'And we need the chips so we're going to build the Terafab.'

key_facts.fact: The facility will be built near Tesla's Giga Texas campus and will vertically integrate chip design, lithography, fabrication, memory production, advanced packaging, and testing — a capability no company outside legacy semiconductor firms currently possesses.
key_facts.excerpt: The $20 billion 'Terafab' plant will be built near Tesla's campus and gigafactory in eastern Travis County.

stories.headline: Cursor Admits Composer 2 Is Built on Moonshot AI's Kimi K2.5, Sparking License Dispute

key_facts.fact: Cursor launched Composer 2 on March 19 as a proprietary frontier-level coding model, but developer @fynnso discovered the internal model ID 'kimi-k2p5-rl-0317-s515-fast' — revealing it was Kimi K2.5 with reinforcement learning applied.
key_facts.excerpt: A developer intercepted the API call and discovered the exact model ID: kimi-k2p5-rl-0317-s515-fast. The name reveals it: it's the Kimi K2.5 with reinforcement learning (RL) on top.

key_facts.fact: Moonshot AI's head of pretraining Yulun Du tested the tokenizer and confirmed it was 'completely identical to our Kimi tokenizer,' publicly questioning Cursor co-founder Michael Truell about licensing compliance before deleting his posts.
key_facts.excerpt: Moonshot AI's pretraining lead Du Yulun immediately tweeted that after testing Composer 2's tokenizer, they found it to be 'completely identical to our Kimi tokenizer,' and 'almost certain that this is our model further retrained.'

key_facts.fact: Cursor VP Lee Robinson confirmed: 'KIMI K2.5. Yes, that's the base we used,' claiming about one-quarter of compute came from the base model with the rest being Cursor's own training. The company asserts compliance through inference partner Fireworks.
key_facts.excerpt: Lee Robinson, VP of Developer Education at Cursor, openly confirmed: 'KIMI K2.5. Yes, that's the base we used.' According to him, only about 1/4 of the compute was from the base model, with the rest being their own training.

key_facts.fact: Kimi K2.5's Modified MIT license requires commercial products with over $20 million in monthly revenue or over 100 million users to prominently display 'Kimi K2.5' in the interface — a threshold Cursor, valued at $29.3 billion and seeking a $50 billion valuation, almost certainly triggers.
key_facts.excerpt: Kimi K2.5 uses a modified MIT license, explicitly stating that commercial products with over 100 million active users or over $20 million in monthly revenue must prominently display 'Kimi K2.5' in the user interface.

key_facts.fact: Kimi K2.5 is a 1 trillion parameter model trained with 15 trillion tokens, developed by Beijing-based Moonshot AI (backed by Alibaba and HongShan). The controversy has fueled debate about whether AI coding startups built on VS Code forks and open-source models justify billion-dollar valuations.
key_facts.excerpt: The Kimi K2.5 is a 1 trillion parameter model trained with 15 trillion tokens. Moonshot made it open to foster the ecosystem. Meanwhile, discussions are blowing up on Hacker News and Reddit.

stories.headline: Tesla, SpaceX, and xAI Unveil $25B Terafab Chip Factory Targeting 1 Terawatt Annual Output

key_facts.fact: Elon Musk officially launched the Terafab project on March 21 at the defunct Seaholm Power Plant in Austin, Texas — a $25 billion joint venture between Tesla, SpaceX, and xAI to build the largest chip fabrication facility ever, consolidating chip design, lithography, fabrication, memory production, advanced packaging, and testing under one roof.
key_facts.excerpt: Musk took the stage at the defunct Seaholm Power Plant in Austin on March 21 to officially launch the project, calling it 'the most epic chip building exercise in history by far.'

key_facts.fact: Terafab targets 2-nanometer process technology with an initial output of 100,000 wafer starts per month, scaling to 1 million wafer starts — roughly 70% of TSMC's entire current global output — and producing 100 to 200 billion custom AI and memory chips annually.
key_facts.excerpt: Terafab is designed for an initial output of 100,000 wafer starts per month, with ambitions to scale to 1 million wafer starts per month at full capacity. For context, that full-scale target would represent roughly 70% of TSMC's entire current global output.

key_facts.fact: Tesla's fifth-generation AI5 chip, the first product Terafab is designed to produce, delivers a 50x total improvement over the AI4 generation with 10x raw compute increase and 9x memory capacity. A separate D3 chip will be built specifically for SpaceX's orbital satellite constellation.
key_facts.excerpt: Tesla claims its new AI5 chip delivers a 50x total improvement over the previous AI4 generation, with 10x raw compute increase and 9x memory capacity.

key_facts.fact: Musk stated that 80% of Terafab's output will be directed toward space-based orbital AI satellites, with 20% for terrestrial applications including Tesla robotaxis and Optimus humanoid robots, which alone require 100–200 GW of chips.
key_facts.excerpt: Elon Musk's stated goal is one terawatt of computing power annually, split between Tesla's AI5 inference chips for vehicles and Optimus robots, and D3 chips built specifically for SpaceXAI's orbital satellite constellation.

key_facts.fact: Musk framed the project as essential, saying current global fabrication produces only 2% of what his companies require and warning that chip supply from TSMC, Samsung, and Micron will hit a ceiling within 3–4 years.
key_facts.excerpt: Musk acknowledged: 'We're very grateful to our existing supply chain, to Samsung, TSMC, Micron and others,' adding 'but there's a maximum rate at which they're comfortable expanding... we need the chips, so we're going to build the Terafab.'

key_facts.fact: Analysts are skeptical: Bernstein's Stacy Rasgon said 'I suspect this is actually harder than sending rockets to Mars,' and Electrek compared the announcement to Tesla's Battery Day 2020 promises, noting the 4680 battery cell program achieved only ~2% of original volume goals.
key_facts.excerpt: Stacy Rasgon (Bernstein): 'It's Musk, so I would never count it out. But I suspect this is actually harder than sending rockets to Mars.'

stories.headline: US Space Force Switches GPS III-8 Launch From Troubled Vulcan Centaur to SpaceX Falcon 9

key_facts.fact: The U.S. Space Force announced it is shifting the GPS III-8 satellite launch from United Launch Alliance's Vulcan Centaur rocket to SpaceX's Falcon 9, due to ongoing solid rocket booster anomalies detected on Vulcan Centaur during two of its four flights since its January 2024 debut.
key_facts.excerpt: The U.S. Space Force has announced a change in plans for its upcoming GPS III-8 satellite launch, shifting the mission to SpaceX's Falcon 9 rocket due to ongoing technical issues with the Vulcan Centaur rocket.

key_facts.fact: Col. Ryan Hiserote, commander of Space Systems Command System Delta 80, said: 'With this change, we are answering the call for rapid delivery of advanced GPS capability while the Vulcan anomaly investigation continues.' The launch is now targeted for no earlier than late April 2026 from Cape Canaveral.
key_facts.excerpt: 'With this change, we are answering the call for rapid delivery of advanced GPS capability while the Vulcan anomaly investigation continues', said Col. Ryan Hiserote, commander of Space Systems Command System Delta 80.

key_facts.fact: GPS III-8 is the tenth and final spacecraft in the GPS III series. The Space Force had paused all national security launches on Vulcan Centaur in February to investigate the SRB anomalies, which occurred during the certification flight in October 2024 and the USSF-87 mission last month.
key_facts.excerpt: Vulcan Centaur, ULA's next-generation rocket and successor to the Atlas V, has experienced SRB-related issues during two of its four launches since debuting in January 2024. stories.headline: Trump gives Iran 48-hour ultimatum: reopen Strait of Hormuz or US will 'obliterate' power plants

key_facts.fact: Trump posted on Truth Social Saturday evening demanding Iran 'FULLY OPEN, WITHOUT THREAT, the Strait of Hormuz, within 48 HOURS' or the US will 'hit and obliterate their various POWER PLANTS, STARTING WITH THE BIGGEST ONE FIRST'
key_facts.excerpt: Trump warned the U.S. will 'obliterate' Iranian power plants if it doesn't fully open the Strait of Hormuz within 48 hours

key_facts.fact: The ultimatum was posted at approximately 7:44 PM ET Saturday March 21, setting a deadline of Monday March 23 evening
key_facts.excerpt: White House statement released late on the evening of March 21, 2026

key_facts.fact: The threat marked a dramatic reversal from just 24 hours earlier when Trump floated ending the war without reopening the strait and spoke about 'winding down' operations
key_facts.excerpt: Trump threatens to strike Iran's power plants if Hormuz not open in 48 hours

key_facts.fact: A 22-nation maritime coalition assembled in the Arabian Sea with over 90 warships, 12 submarines, and 400+ naval aircraft — the largest multinational naval force in the Middle East since the 2003 Iraq invasion
key_facts.excerpt: 22-nation maritime coalition assembled the largest naval force in the region since the 2003 Iraq invasion

key_facts.fact: Trump demanded Iran withdraw all IRGCN vessels from the waterway, remove all naval mines deployed since Feb. 28, restore AIS transponder coverage, and permit unimpeded transit
key_facts.excerpt: Withdraw all IRGCN vessels from waterway, remove/neutralize all naval mines deployed since Feb. 28, restore AIS transponder coverage, permit unimpeded transit

stories.headline: US considers ground operation to seize Iran's Kharg Island oil hub; 4,500 Marines deploying

key_facts.fact: Senior US officials informed Israeli and other allied counterparts that there may be 'no alternative' but to launch a ground military operation to seize Iran's Kharg Island
key_facts.excerpt: Senior US officials have informed their counterparts in Israel and other nations in recent days that it appears there may be no alternative but for the United States to launch a ground military operation to seize the Iranian island of Kharg

key_facts.fact: Kharg Island handles 90% of Iran's crude oil exports, with most oil destined for China, making it a critical economic pressure point
key_facts.excerpt: Located in the Persian Gulf, Kharg Island serves as Iran's primary hub for oil exports, with 90% of its crude oil destined for China

key_facts.fact: The USS Boxer Amphibious Readiness Group with approximately 4,500 Marines and additional combat personnel has been deployed to the region, including amphibious assault ship USS Boxer, USS Portland, and USS Comstock
key_facts.excerpt: USS Boxer Amphibious Readiness Group deployed... approximately 4,500 Marines and additional combat personnel

key_facts.fact: Nearly 5,000 personnel from the 31st and 11th US Marine Expeditionary Units are moving toward the Strait of Hormuz, and US Army Special Forces from the 82nd Airborne Division are preparing to deploy
key_facts.excerpt: Nearly 5,000 personnel from the 31st and 11th U.S. Marine Expeditionary Units are moving toward the Strait of Hormuz... 82nd Airborne Division are preparing to deploy

key_facts.fact: The Christian Science Monitor reported the Trump administration is considering occupying Kharg Island to gain negotiating leverage with Tehran as gas prices rise at a record-setting pace
key_facts.excerpt: As gas prices rise at a record-setting pace, the Trump administration is reportedly considering sending U.S. troops to occupy Kharg Island, Iran's main oil export hub

stories.headline: Saudi Arabia expels Iran's military attache and embassy staff over continued attacks

key_facts.fact: Saudi Arabia declared Iran's military attache, his assistant, and three embassy staff members persona non grata and ordered them to leave within 24 hours
key_facts.excerpt: Saudi Arabia informed Iran's military attache, his assistant and three members of the embassy staff that they must leave the kingdom within 24 hours after being declared persona non grata

key_facts.fact: Saudi Arabia has come under attack by hundreds of Iranian missiles and drones since the start of the US-Israeli war with Iran, the vast majority of which have been intercepted
key_facts.excerpt: Saudi Arabia has come under attack by hundreds of Iranian missiles and drones since the start of U.S.-Israeli war on Iran, the vast majority of which have been intercepted

key_facts.fact: Three ballistic missiles were detected around Riyadh early Sunday; one was intercepted and two fell in an uninhabited area
key_facts.excerpt: One missile was intercepted, while the other two fell in an uninhabited area

key_facts.fact: The move follows Qatar's similar decision earlier in the week to declare Iran's security and military attache persona non grata, and puts the 2023 Beijing-brokered Saudi-Iran normalization deal in question
key_facts.excerpt: The decision, announced by the Saudi foreign ministry, follows a similar move by Qatar... brings into question the future of the Beijing-brokered 2023 Riyadh-Tehran normalization agreement

key_facts.fact: The Saudi foreign ministry warned that continued Iranian attacks would lead to further escalation and have 'significant consequences' for current and future relations
key_facts.excerpt: Iran's continued targeting of Saudi territory, civilian infrastructure, economic interests, and diplomatic premises constitutes a 'clear violation' of international law

stories.headline: Ukraine-US peace talks conclude in Florida without Russia; Zelensky says Iran war dominates US focus

key_facts.fact: Ukrainian and US delegations held two days of talks in Florida on March 21-22, led by US special envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, to discuss ways to end the four-year Russia-Ukraine war
key_facts.excerpt: U.S. and Ukrainian officials met in Miami on March 22 for a second day of talks aimed at brokering a peace deal with Moscow

key_facts.fact: Russian representatives were absent from the talks, which were originally expected to take place in Abu Dhabi with Moscow's participation before being moved due to the Iran war
key_facts.excerpt: Russian representatives were not present at the talks, which opened in Florida... They were originally expected to attend the negotiations, which were expected to take place in Abu Dhabi

key_facts.fact: Zelensky acknowledged that 'the U.S. side's attention at the moment is focused primarily on the situation around Iran' and expressed a 'very bad feeling' about the consequences of the Iran conflict for Ukraine
key_facts.excerpt: It is clear that the U.S. side's attention at the moment is focused primarily on the situation around Iran

key_facts.fact: Zelensky signaled progress on prisoner-of-war exchanges following the talks, though details of broader negotiations were not disclosed
key_facts.excerpt: Zelensky said in his evening address that he had received a report on the discussions

key_facts.fact: Washington temporarily lifted some sanctions on Russian oil to help cope with supply shortages caused by the Iran war
key_facts.excerpt: Washington has temporarily lifted some sanctions on Russian oil to help cope with supply shortages caused by war in Iran

stories.headline: S&P 500 closes fourth straight losing week as oil hits $112; traders abandon Fed rate-cut bets

key_facts.fact: The S&P 500 fell 1.5% to 6,506.48 on Friday, closing its fourth consecutive losing week — its longest such streak in a year

key_facts.excerpt: The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 443 points, or 1%, and the Nasdaq composite tumbled 2%

key_facts.excerpt: Brent crude, the international standard, rose 3.3% to settle at $112.19 per barrel. Benchmark U.S. crude gained 2.3% to $98.32 per barrel

stories.headline: Canada to cut 12,000+ federal jobs over three years in Carney government spending review

key_facts.fact: Federal departments and agencies plan to cut more than 12,000 full-time equivalent positions over the next three years as part of the Carney government's comprehensive spending review
key_facts.excerpt: Federal departments and agencies are looking to cut more than 12,000 full-time equivalent jobs over the next three years as part of the Carney government's spending review

key_facts.fact: Major cuts include 1,793 positions at Public Services and Procurement Canada, 900 at Statistics Canada, and 942 at Health Canada
key_facts.excerpt: Among the expected job losses are 1,793 positions at Public Services and Procurement Canada, 900 jobs at Statistics Canada and 942 at Health Canada

key_facts.fact: The cuts are part of a broader plan from Canada Strong Budget 2025 to eliminate 28,000 federal positions by 2029 and find up to 15% in savings across 90 departments
key_facts.excerpt: The Canada Strong Budget 2025 outlined a plan to reduce the size of the federal public service by 28,000 positions by 2029, and directed departments to find up to 15 per cent in savings

stories.headline: FDA approves nivolumab + chemo as first-line treatment for advanced Hodgkin lymphoma

key_facts.fact: The FDA approved nivolumab (Opdivo) combined with AVD chemotherapy (doxorubicin, vinblastine, dacarbazine) as a first-line treatment for adults and children 12+ with stage III or IV classical Hodgkin lymphoma
key_facts.excerpt: The Food and Drug Administration has approved a new first-line treatment option for adults and children aged 12 years and older with stage III or IV classical Hodgkin lymphoma

key_facts.fact: In the phase 3 SWOG S1826 trial of 994 patients, adding nivolumab to AVD reduced the risk of disease progression or death by 58% compared to brentuximab vedotin plus AVD (hazard ratio 0.42)
key_facts.excerpt: Adding nivolumab to AVD reduced the risk of disease progression or death by 58% compared to brentuximab vedotin plus AVD

key_facts.fact: After a median follow-up of 36.7 months, the death rate was 1.8% in the nivolumab group versus 3.4% in the comparator group
key_facts.excerpt: After 36.7-month median follow-up: 1.8% deaths in nivolumab group versus 3.4% in comparison group

key_facts.fact: The drug is manufactured by Bristol Myers Squibb and is administered at 240 mg intravenously for patients 40 kg or above, on days 1 and 15 of 28-day cycles for a maximum of six cycles
key_facts.excerpt: 240 mg intravenously for patients ≥40 kg; 3 mg/kg for those <40 kg, administered on days 1 and 15 of 28-day cycles (maximum six cycles)

key_facts.fact: The approval also converted two previous accelerated approvals for nivolumab in post-transplant and heavily pre-treated Hodgkin lymphoma populations to traditional approvals
key_facts.excerpt: The approval also converted two previous accelerated approvals to traditional approvals for post-transplant and heavily pre-treated patient populations

sources.title: FDA Approves Nivolumab Combo as First-Line Hodgkin Lymphoma Treatment

stories.headline: Large VA study finds stopping GLP-1 drugs rapidly reverses cardiovascular protection

key_facts.fact: A large Veterans Affairs study analyzing over 174,000 patients over a decade found that GLP-1 receptor agonist use was associated with a 15% reduced risk of major cardiovascular events
key_facts.excerpt: GLP-1RA initiation associated with lower risks of major cardiovascular events and end-stage kidney disease

key_facts.fact: The study, published in Nature Medicine, found a 19% reduced risk of end-stage kidney disease in patients using GLP-1 receptor agonists
key_facts.excerpt: Patients using GLP-1RAs demonstrated a 15% reduced risk of major cardiovascular events and a 19% reduced risk of end-stage kidney disease

key_facts.fact: Critically, the cardiovascular protective benefits erode rapidly once patients stop taking GLP-1 drugs, raising concerns about long-term adherence, cost barriers, and supply shortages
key_facts.excerpt: Stopping GLP-1 Drugs Rapidly Reverses Heart Protection, Large VA Study Finds

key_facts.fact: GLP-1 use was not associated with increased hospitalizations for diabetic ketoacidosis or severe hypoglycemia, allaying key safety concerns
key_facts.excerpt: GLP-1RA use not associated with more hospitalizations for diabetic ketoacidosis or severe hypoglycemia

key_facts.fact: Patients using GLP-1 receptor agonists were more likely to achieve clinically meaningful weight loss, though randomized controlled trials are still needed to confirm the observational findings
key_facts.excerpt: Patients using GLP-1RAs more likely to achieve clinically meaningful weight loss... Findings are promising, but randomized trials are still needed because the study is observational
